title: Display output
contrast: Python's print() ends the line for you. Java has println() to end the line and print() to stay on it.

title: Comments
contrast: Python uses # and docstrings. Java uses //, /* */, and /** */ Javadoc.

title: Variables
contrast: Python figures out the type from the value, and a name can later hold a different type. Java makes you declare the type, and that variable's type never changes.

title: Data types
contrast: Python has int, float, str, bool. Java has primitives (int, double, char, boolean) plus objects like String.

title: Read user input
contrast: Python's input() always returns a string. Java's Scanner has a separate method for each type.

title: Math operators
contrast: In Python, 7 / 2 is 3.5 and 7 // 2 is 3. In Java, 7 / 2 is 3 because both values are ints.

title: Comparisons and logic
contrast: Python spells logic as and, or, not. Java uses &&, ||, !.

title: Make decisions
contrast: Python uses elif and indentation. Java uses else if, parentheses, and braces.

title: Count with a for loop
contrast: Python loops over range(). Java's for header has three parts: start; condition; update.

title: Repeat with while
contrast: Same idea in both. Java needs parentheses around the condition and braces around the body.

title: Lists and arrays
contrast: A Python list can grow. A Java array has a fixed size set when you create it.

title: Functions and methods
contrast: Python uses def with no types. Java methods live inside a class and declare a return type and parameter types.

title: Return a value
contrast: Python functions return None if they reach the end without return. A Java method declares its return type, and a non-void method must return a value of that type on every path.

title: String basics
contrast: Python uses len(s) and ==. Java uses s.length() and s.equals(other).

title: Read an error message
contrast: Python reports syntax errors before running but type mistakes only when that line runs. Java's compiler catches both before the program runs. A bad index crashes both while running.

title: Your first class
contrast: Python creates fields inside __init__ with self. Java declares fields at the top of the class, and a no-argument constructor sets each one to a starting value.

title: Parameterized constructor
contrast: Python allows only one __init__, so default parameter values let it work with or without arguments. Java writes a second constructor with parameters, so a class can have both a default and a parameterized constructor.

title: Accessor and mutator methods
contrast: Java marks fields private, and the compiler blocks access from outside the class. Python marks them with a leading underscore by convention only. In both, mutators usually return nothing.

title: The this keyword
contrast: Python always writes self.field. Java needs this.field only when a parameter has the same name as the field.

title: String methods
contrast: Strings are immutable in both. Python slices with s[1:4]; Java uses s.substring(1, 4).

title: Format output
contrast: Python uses f-strings. Java uses printf or String.format with codes like %.2f.

title: Grow and change a list
contrast: Python's list does it all. Java switches from arrays to ArrayList when the size needs to change.

title: break and continue
contrast: Both languages use the same keywords. Python also has for...else, which runs when the loop never hits break.

title: Nested loops
contrast: Same structure in both. Indentation shows the nesting in Python; braces show it in Java.

title: 2D lists and arrays
contrast: Python builds a grid as a list of lists. Java declares int[][], an array of arrays whose sizes are set when you create it.

title: Key-value maps
contrast: Python's dict uses d[key]. Java's HashMap uses put() and get().

title: Multiple parameters and returns
contrast: Python can return several values as a tuple. A Java method returns one value of its declared type.

title: Variable scope
contrast: In Python, a variable made inside an if or loop still exists after it, as long as that code ran. In Java, a variable lives only inside its braces.

title: Handle errors
contrast: Python uses try/except. Java uses try/catch, and the compiler forces you to handle checked exceptions.

title: Read and write files
contrast: Python's with block closes the file. Java's try-with-resources does the same job.

title: Random numbers
contrast: Python's randint(1, 6) includes 6. Java's nextInt(6) gives 0 to 5, so you add 1.

title: Math library
contrast: Python needs import math. Java's Math class is always available.

title: Overloaded constructors and this()
contrast: Java can overload several constructors and chain them with this(...). Python has one __init__ and uses default parameter values instead.

title: Encapsulation
contrast: Python marks private data with a leading underscore and uses @property. Java enforces private and uses getters and setters.

title: Class vs instance members
contrast: Python class variables sit in the class body. Java marks them static.

title: Print and compare objects
contrast: Python uses __str__ and __eq__. Java overrides toString() and equals().

title: Inheritance
contrast: Python writes class Dog(Animal). Java writes class Dog extends Animal.

title: Polymorphism and overriding
contrast: Python checks methods at run time (duck typing). Java checks that the declared type has the method at compile time.

title: Abstract classes and interfaces
contrast: Python uses ABC and @abstractmethod. Java has abstract classes and a separate interface keyword.

title: Recursion
contrast: Same logic in both. Python stops at about 1000 calls deep by default; Java's limit depends on stack size.

title: Linear and binary search
contrast: Same algorithms. Python uses // for the midpoint; Java's int division does it automatically.

title: Selection and insertion sort
contrast: Python swaps with a, b = b, a. Java needs a temporary variable.

title: Draw shapes
contrast: Python's turtle draws by moving a pen. Java's Swing draws inside paintComponent with a Graphics object.

title: Mouse and keyboard events
contrast: Python's turtle registers callback functions. Java adds listener objects to a component.

title: Merge sort
contrast: Python slices make new lists easily. Java usually passes index ranges to avoid copying arrays.

title: Measure growth with Big-O
contrast: Both languages count steps the same way. To time code, Python uses time.perf_counter() and Java uses System.nanoTime(), but timings change on every run.

title: Memoization and dynamic programming
contrast: Python can memoize with @functools.cache. Java stores results in a HashMap or array by hand.

title: Build a linked list
contrast: Python nodes point with None at the end. Java uses null and a typed Node class.

title: Stacks and queues
contrast: Python uses list and collections.deque. Java uses ArrayDeque for both.

title: Sets and hashing
contrast: Python objects in a set need __hash__ and __eq__; defining only __eq__ makes them unhashable. Java objects need hashCode() and equals(); with only equals(), the set keeps duplicates and reports no error.

title: Generics and type hints
contrast: Python type hints are not enforced when the program runs. Java generics are checked by the compiler.

title: Custom sort order
contrast: Python passes key= to sorted(). Java implements Comparable or passes a Comparator.

title: Lambdas, map, and filter
contrast: Python favors list comprehensions. Java uses lambdas with the Stream API.

title: Iterators and generators
contrast: Python's yield builds an iterator in a few lines. Java implements the Iterator interface with hasNext() and next().

title: Data classes and records
contrast: Python's @dataclass writes __init__, __repr__, and __eq__, and frozen=True makes it unchangeable and hashable. Java's record writes the constructor, getters, toString(), equals(), and hashCode(), and its fields can never be reassigned.

title: Strategy pattern
contrast: Python can pass plain functions as strategies. Java defines an interface, often filled with a lambda.

title: Threads and shared data
contrast: Python uses threading.Lock. Java uses synchronized or classes from java.util.concurrent.

title: Test your code
contrast: Python ships unittest in the standard library. Java projects add JUnit; this example uses plain checks so it runs anywhere.

title: Animation and game loop
contrast: Python's turtle schedules frames with ontimer(). Java's Swing uses a javax.swing.Timer and repaint().
